object_types.name: Reviewer
object_types.definition: A person who reviews papers for the conference.

source_references.excerpt: Reviewers review papers. A reviewer can review many papers... Reviewers have a reviewer ID.

object_types.name: Paper
object_types.definition: A submitted manuscript for the conference.

source_references.excerpt: Reviewers review papers... Papers have a paper number.

object_types.name: Review
object_types.definition: The act of a reviewer reviewing a paper, tracked as a distinct entity with its own review ID.

source_references.excerpt: Each completed review gets its own review ID -- we treat the review itself as a thing we track... The review is the act of a particular reviewer reviewing a particular paper.

objectified_fact_types.description: The relationship between Reviewer and Paper is objectified as Review. This allows the review itself to be tracked as a distinct entity with its own identifier and attributes (such as review score), rather than treating the relationship as a simple link.

source_references.excerpt: Each completed review gets its own review ID -- we treat the review itself as a thing we track... The review is the act of a particular reviewer reviewing a particular paper -- the score hangs off that pairing, not off the paper alone.

ambiguities.description: Identification of Reviewer and Paper: The transcript states 'Reviewers have a reviewer ID' and 'Papers have a paper number' but does not explicitly confirm these are the only identifiers or whether they are universally unique. Is reviewer_id globally unique, or only within a conference instance?

source_references.excerpt: Reviewers have a reviewer ID. Papers have a paper number.

ambiguities.description: Participation constraints on Reviewer and Paper roles: The transcript states 'a given reviewer reviews a given paper at most once' but does not explicitly state that every reviewer must review at least one paper, or that every paper must be reviewed by at least one reviewer. Are there mandatory constraints on the 'is reviewed by' or 'performs' roles?

ambiguities.description: Review score constraint placement: ReviewScore is defined as a value type with a fixed constraint (values 1-5), but it is unclear whether this constraint applies universally to all ReviewScore values or only in the context of Review. Should the value_constraint be on the ReviewScore object type itself, or on the role within the 'Review has ReviewScore' fact type?
